mechanism_narrative: A federal funds rate below 0.5% indicates an accommodative monetary policy stance that reduces discount rates for equity cash flows, producing positive S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days as investors anticipate sustained low-cost capital.
failure_condition: SPX 20-day returns are negative in more than 55% of periods when FEDFUNDS is below 0.5%, or Rank IC falls below 0.05 over any 3-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained unemployment rate exceeding 9.5% for two consecutive months signals deteriorating labor market conditions that precede corporate earnings declines, causing negative S&P 500 returns over the next 5 trading days.
failure_condition: When UNRATE exceeds 9.5% for two consecutive months, SPX 5-day returns are positive in more than 55% of instances.

mechanism_narrative: Simultaneous declines in housing starts (HOUST) and real personal consumption (RSAFS) indicate broad-based demand contraction that triggers recession fears, producing negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
candidate_trigger: HOUST and RSAFS both decline from prior month
failure_condition: When HOUST and RSAFS both decline from prior month, SPX 60-day returns are positive in more than 55% of cases.

mechanism_narrative: Declining industrial production (INDPRO < 100) combined with rising inflation (CPIAUCSL > 2.5%) defines a stagflationary regime where profit margins compress, causing negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: In periods with INDPRO < 100 and CPIAUCSL > 2.5%, SPX 20-day returns are positive in more than 55% of instances.

mechanism_narrative: A monthly CPI increase exceeding 0.3% signals accelerating inflation that triggers hawkish monetary policy expectations, producing negative S&P 500 returns over the next 5 trading days as rate hike fears intensify.
failure_condition: When CPIAUCSL monthly change exceeds 0.3%, SPX 5-day returns are positive in more than 55% of cases.

mechanism_narrative: Sustained non-farm payroll growth above 100,000 per month indicates a strengthening labor market that supports consumer spending and corporate earnings, producing positive S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX 60-day returns are negative in more than 55% of periods when PAYEMS growth exceeds 100,000, or Rank IC falls below 0.05 over 3-year windows.

mechanism_narrative: A quarterly real GDP decline below 0.5% annualized rate signals economic contraction that triggers recession expectations, causing negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: When GDPC1 quarterly growth falls below 0.5%, SPX 20-day returns are positive in more than 55% of instances.

mechanism_narrative: Simultaneous increases in federal funds rate (FEDFUNDS) and inflation (CPIAUCSL) signal a monetary tightening cycle that pressures equity valuations, producing negative S&P 500 returns over the next 5 trading days.
candidate_trigger: FEDFUNDS increases and CPIAUCSL increases from prior month
failure_condition: When FEDFUNDS increases and CPIAUCSL increases from prior month, SPX 5-day returns are positive in more than 55% of cases.
